chunks: To how many habitations did We give respite, though given to wickedness, and then seized them. To Me they had to come back in the end.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean by giving respite to sinful cities before destruction?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Hajj illustrates the divine attribute of 'Imla' (giving respite), where God prolongs the life of oppressive communities not out of approval, but to allow their sins to accumulate and their punishment to be severe. It serves as a historical reminder of cities like Ad and Thamud, reinforcing the concept that ultimate return (al-Masir) is to Allah, who will hold them accountable for their transgressions.
